26. HEADACHE IN PREGNANCY
•85 different types of headaches are there
• 90 % headaches are Migraine and Tension type.

History:

•Duration.
•Severity.
•Frequency.
•Location.
•Fx.
•Association with pregnancy.
•Red flag feature assessment.

Examination:

•B. P Fundoscopy:
•Neurological Papilledema, raised ICP

Examination. CNS – Examination:

•Proteinuria - Pupil reaction.
•Clonus - Visual acuity.

- Eye movement CN (6).

- Speech, swallowing.

 

Tone, power, reflexes coordination.

 

Planter response.

 

Gait assessment.

Causes of Headache:

Primary Secondary

1.Migraine. 1. HTN.
2.Tension. 2. SAH.

3. Drugs nifedipine.

4. post Dural.

5. Stroke.

6. Meningitis.

7. Caffeine withdrawal.

8. Anemia.

9. ICH.

10. AVM.

11. Tumors enlargement.

12. Bleeding in tumor.

13. Mets.

Red Flag Features:

1.Thunder clap:
-Rapid peaking in seconds and minutes (SAH).
-Sudden shape headache
- become vitally unstable
2.Focal Neurological Symptoms:
-Limb weakness, Aura – <5min, >1hour.
3.Non – Focal CVT:
-Cognitive disturbance.
4.Abnormal Neurological Examination.
5.Change in Frequency/ characteristics.
6.Postural Headache.
7.Headache awakening the patient.
8.Headache with physical exertion.
9.Jaw claudication;
-Age > 50, Giant cell arteritis.
10.Fever meningitis.
11.Neck stiffness.
12.New onset headache:
-HIV.
-CA.
⇨Post Dural puncture Headache:
•0.5 – 2% of epidurals.
•Accidental puncture – 70 – 80% experience headache.
•Peak @24 – 48hours last for 7 – 10 days. May last up to 6weeks.
•Treatment:
-Conservative – hydration, analgesic.
-Epidural blood patch – 60 – 90% cure.

 

⇨Migraine:
-With Aura – worsen in pregnancy.
-Without Aura – improves.

Aura: reversible phenomenon of visual sensation, motor power, Balance and speech (5 – 6min).

Treatment:

1st line – avoidance of triggers.

- Rest hydration, regular meals, relaxation.

⇨Paracetamol
⇨2nd line:
-5HT1 – receptor Agonists triptans sumatriptan.
-NSAIDS.

After informed discussion of Pt.

Prophylaxis if 3 – 4 episodes/months.

1.Propranolol – 20 – 40mg TDS.
2.Amitriptyline 25 – 50mg.

Migraine:

-2 times risk of pre-eclampsia.
-4 times risk of Myocardial infarction
-17 times risk of stroke.

 

⇨Idiopathic Intracranial HTN:
•0.9/100,000.
•Male: Female.
•1: 8.
•Obese women 19/100,000
•Generalized, non-throbbing, aggregated by Valsalva i-e coughing + eye movements.
•Diplopia 38%, visual loss 31%, Retro bulbar 6th nerve palsy.

MDT:

•Ophthalmologist.
•Neurologist.
•Obstetrician.
•Anaesthetist.

Diagnosis by Dandy criteria:

•Exclude other causes by CT.
•I/C pressure on lumber puncture > 20cm of water

Management:

•Weight loss or limit weight gain maximum 20 pounds in pregnancy.
•Monitoring of visual field & visual acuity – risk of optic nerve infarction.
•Therapeutic LP. Limit visual loss &

•Acetazolamide 5mg B.D improve headache.
•Steroids. - S/A – Safe.

- G/A – risky - pressure

Surgical:

•Optical nerve fenestration.
•Lumbo peritoneal shunting.
⇨Cerebral Venous Thrombosis:
-3rd and 4 weeks PP, worst ever headache.
-Most common site cerebral cortical veins.

S/S:

-Headache 80 – 90%.
-Papilledema, focal deficient, altered consciousness, seizures, neurological signs, psychosis.

Diagnosis:

-MRV.
-CT – not sensitive detects 30% of CVT.

Management:

-Prompt referral to neurologist.
-LMWH – 6m0.
-Endovascular therapy if coma.
-F/U MRV 3 – 6m0.
-Thrombophilia Screening.

 

⇨Cluster Headache:
•Watery red eye.
•Dropping eyelids.
•Severe throbbing pain.
•Multiple attacks over few weeks, then symptoms free for years or months.
•Attacks @ same time of the day daily.
•Awaken the person from sleep.
⇨Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES):

Clinical – Radiological – neurological entity associated with Pre – eclampsia due to Failed Autoregulation.

Clinical=>nausea, vomiting, seizures, altered mental state and headache.

Radiological=>edema in posterior circulation of brain.

Neurological=>altered sensorium

PRES without HTN:

•SLE.
•Sepsis
•Immunosuppressants drug use.
•Nephrotic syndrome.

Treatment:

-As severe PE + delivery of baby.
⇨Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction Syndrome:
•More in PP period
• Worst headache
•Recurrent, Sudden, Severe headache over 1 – 3weeks.

Treatment:

-Take expert opinion, ca – channel blocker, high dose steroid, mgso4.

Imaging in Pregnancy:

•CT recommended fetal expose < 0.005Mgy (accepted in pregnancy cumulative dose 50Mgy).
•MRI recommended
•Gadolinium recommended
•Contrast media containing element iodine not recommended.

If used Neonatal thyroid function should be checked.
